item.title: TD says Killarney is being hollowed out and short term lets U-turn is not a win for the town
item.description: A Kerry TD believes the changes to short-term let restrictions should not be framed as a win for Killarney. The government proposals were initially set to cover towns with populations above 10,000, which would have included Killarney. However, it will now only apply to towns with populations of over 20,000, which would include Tralee. item.title: Council gives go-ahead for 27 new houses in Ballybunion
item.description: Kerry County Council has given the go-ahead for 27 new houses in Ballybunion. ACG Ventures LTD trading as Atlantic Golf Construction applied for planning permission to build the houses behind St John’s Church in the town. The housing development will include six one-bedroom houses and two, two-bedroom homes. Advertisement There will also be 15 three-bed homes and four, four-bed houses. item.title: Listenership to Radio Kerry increases to record levels
item.description: Listenership to Radio Kerry has grown to record levels. The latest JNLR radio listenership figures show that the stations market share has grown from 54% to 57.2%. Radio Kerry now has a weekly reach of 90,000 listeners in Kerry. Advertisement Almost 3.5 million adults tune into radio each weekday, underlining radio’s continued strength and relevance in a changing media landscape according to Radio Centre Ireland. item.title: Kerry company told it’s lucky workplace injury didn’t lead to death as judge hands down fine
item.description: A Kerry company has been told had a workplace accident been more serious, a custodial sentence would likely have been handed down. Judge David Waters made the statement during his ruling at a recent sitting of Tralee District Court. Clifford Brothers Ardfert Potatoes Ltd and Noel Clifford were before the court facing charges relating to an incident in July 2024 at Snipefield, Kilmoyley. item.title: Kerry County Councillor says fines may need to be issued to landowners who fail to cut roadside hedges
item.description: A Kerry County Councillor says fines may need to be issued to landowners who fail to cut their roadside hedges. Kerry Independent Alliance councillor John O'Donoghue says the system of issuing property owners with letters telling them to cut their hedges is being widely ignored. The Road Safety Authority has called on landowners to cut hedgerows by the end of this month to ensure they're not causing a road safety hazard. item.title: New Killarney Community Nursing Unit to open “in next few weeks”
item.description: The chief executive of the HSE has said Killarney Community Nursing Unit will open in the next few weeks. He was answering a question by Deputy Michael Cahill at the Joint Oireachtas Committee on Health. The Health Service Executive’s (HSE) Bernard Gloster told the committee that the new Ballydribbeen facility will open in the first quarter of this year. item.title: First section of the new Tralee Northern Relief Road to open next week
item.description: The first section of the new Tralee Northern Relief Road will open next week. The 1.25km of road will open from Forge Cross Roundabout to the newly-constructed roundabout at Listellick on the Tralee to Abbeydorney road. This stretch provides a link to the Tralee bypass and MTU Kerry campus, while adjacent cycleway and walkway along the entire route are included. item.title: Basketball Preview
item.description: In Basketball Ireland National League Division One, Killarney Cougars host Utility Trust St Paul’s Killarney Lakers at the Presentation Gym in Killarney. Tip-off is at 8pm, with doors open from 7.30pm. There is also extensive Kerry Airport underage action this evening across Under-18, Under-16, Under-14 and Under-12 grades at venues including Moyderwell School, Glenbeigh GAA Sports Hall, Duagh Sports Complex and Nagle Rice College, Milltown.
